verdict.rationale: Gecko documents an API and MCP-based path (not a CLI) to trigger scans, pull machine-readable vulnerability data, and file tickets in Jira/Linear/etc (gecko-security-docs-9, gecko-security-docs-10, gecko-security-docs-6), which is the closest analog to a headless CI workflow, but there is no evidence of an actual CLI tool. More critically, hands-on community testing directly contradicts the 'real findings' premise: the tool gave 100% confidence on two vulnerabilities that weren't real, missed a real vulnerability another scanner caught, and flagged a trivial/irrelevant issue as RCE (gecko-security-comm-3, gecko-security-comm-4, gecko-security-comm-5). missing for 10: a documented CLI for headless scanning, independent verification that filed issues correspond to real (not false-positive) findings, and evidence of reliable automated ticket-filing in practice.
